plans.covers: Warehouse atta corrections: net is the sum of signed value at cost and gross is the sum of absolute values.

S8N17.cannot: Mirror-image pairing needs two rows of the same correction table compared to each other, but a table can appear only once per plan and no join key links a warehouse correction to a store count adjustment; the two correction types also live in different units (dc-stock-adjustments.cases versus stock-counts.adjustment in packs), so the within-15%-in-cases test cannot be planned without inventing a conversion or a self-join.

S8N18.cannot: The records do not link a goods receipt to the stock it added, so a receipt cannot be followed into a later stock count. goods-receipts-june can be joined to stock-counts-june only by sku, which would compare a product's receipt with a product's count, not show that the received units survived. There is also no recorded definition of 'survive' (units still present, counted quantity, or adjustment), and no batch- or pallet-level stock balance to test it against.

S9N11.cannot: The records hold no OTIF scorecard and no counterfactual: pallets-june shows every pallet 'not weighed' and goods-receipts are booked by pallet-label scan, but nothing records what weighing at dispatch or case scanning at the store would find, so no improvement can be computed. What the records can show is the current evidence such a scorecard would rest on: per shipment, arrived_ts against slot_start/slot_end (on time), dc-pick-confirmations cases_confirmed against cases_ordered (in full), and goods-receipts units_booked against shipping-notice units (what the door scan actually booked).
